text:
maria: Heads up — after today's CUDA driver bump we are seeing kernel-path oscillation on H100 pools for mid-range sequence lengths (~512–768). Latency spikes and KV-cache hit rate dropped on a few routes.

kevin: saw p50/p90 go up on the gpt-medium route too. correlates with a change in kernel selection distribution.

arin: quick diag — can you paste the profiling snippet from the affected pods?

maria: here are a couple lines from the runtime logs (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T17:02:13Z] model=gpt-medium pod=h100-22 kernel_pick=fast_attention_v2 seq_len=640 latency_ms=85 kv_cache_hit=0.62
[2026-03-17T17:02:14Z] model=gpt-medium pod=h100-22 kernel_pick=matmul_streamlined seq_len=640 latency_ms=122 kv_cache_hit=0.18
[2026-03-17T17:02:15Z] model=gpt-medium pod=h100-22 kernel_pick=fast_attention_v2 seq_len=640 latency_ms=88 kv_cache_hit=0.61
```

maria: note the pick flips between `fast_attention_v2` and `matmul_streamlined` within seconds for identical seq_len and batch sizes. KV cache hit drops when path switches.

neel: interesting — driver-level heuristics could be changing GEMM kernel perf characteristics causing our autotuner score to bounce. we've seen similar on driver bumps before.

riley: do we have a simple fallback? e.g., pinning kernel picks for seq_len range or increasing kv cache threshold to avoid path switches under load?

kevin: can we just force the old kernel on the live pool for a quick mitigation? how invasive is a kernel-override at runtime?

arin: we have `autotune.override_rules` that can be applied per-pool without code restart. example: `{"seq_len_range": [512,768], "force_kernel": "fast_attention_v2"}`. Should be low-risk.

maria: I can push that rule to h100-prod-canary.

deploy-bot: deploy request #PR-4782 to set autotune override on h100-prod-canary queued. Approver: @neel.

neel: approving. roll the override to canary then monitor KV hit and latencies for 10m.

kevin: we should also prepare a rollback of the CUDA driver in parallel in case overrides are insufficient. ops, what’s the plan for driver rollback?

riley: rollback requires node-drain and driver reinstall; we have a previous GPU image `nvidia/driver:12.3.1` in the artifact registry. estimated ~8–12m per node, can do canary nodes first.

maria: immediate mitigation deployed to canary. will post metrics in 5m.

sre-bot: alert: p95 latency for gpt-medium increased 35% on h100-prod between 17:01 and 17:07 UTC. Incident channel: #incidents.

maria: initial canary numbers look good — KV cache hit recovered from 0.2 -> 0.63 and p95 dropped ~18%.

neel: ok, plan: (1) propagate kernel-override to 20% of h100-prod, (2) if stable for 30m, roll to 100%, (3) concurrently prepare node-level driver rollback playbook in case we see regressions in other seq ranges.

arin: add a short-term tweak to autotune scoring: increase `kv_cache_weight` to bias picks that preserve cache (config suggestion: `autotune.kv_cache_weight = 1.5` vs default 1.0). Should reduce flip-flopping while we evaluate driver impact.

kevin: who will own the rollback playbook? ops? I can help script the `kubectl drain && apt-get install nvidia-driver=12.3.1` flow and a canary test harness.

riley: ops will own execution, eng-runtime + eng-sre will validate canary. riley -> tagging @kevin for scripts.

maria: filing a short postmortem stub with profiling graphs and the mitigation steps. main action items: kernel-override, autotune-weight tweak, driver rollback playbook, longer-term: make kernel selection less sensitive to micro-bench variance after driver bumps.

neel: add an automated autotune snapshot before any future driver upgrade so we can diff kernel-scores pre/post.

maria: good call — I'll add that to the driver-upgrade checklist.

kevin: thanks all. will follow up with scripts and a canary runbook. :thumbsup:
